newsitem.title: JAPAN: Lending rates of public bodies to rise to 3.1% - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Lending rates of public bodies to rise to 3.1% - MOF.

text.p: The lending rates of government-affiliated financial bodies, such as the Japan Development Bank (JDB), will be raised to 3.1 percent from 2.6 percent, the Finance Ministry (MOF) said on Tuesday.
The increase takes effect on Wednesday, it said.

Lending rates for the People's Finance Corporation, Japan Finance Corporation for Small Business, Hokkaido and Tohoku Development Corporation, Environmental Sanitation Business Finance Corporation and the Japan Development Bank will all be raised to 3.1 percent, MOF said in a statement.
The increase in lending rates was due to a rise in Japan's long-term prime rate, a MOF official said.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) said on Monday it would raise its long-term prime lending rate for May to 3.1 percent, effective from May 14, from 2.5 percent in April.

Government-affiliated financial bodies receive loans from the Fiscal Investment and Loan Programme, which collects funds mainly through postal savings and public pension systems and then funnels them to public agencies.

According to the Bank of Japan, the total outstanding loans of government-affiliated financial institutions, including the JDB, the Export-Import Bank of Japan, nine public finance corporations and the Shokochukin Bank, were worth 149.39 trillion yen as of the end of December 1996.
